flagged.claim: Thm o-ir (iv): the arity-two graphs along (eta1, eta2) in Sigma* x Sigma* converge at large distance, because floating S^(1)(eta) decays as |y|^-5, a special-edge pair as |y|^-6, and S^(2) never floats.
flagged.evidence: The list leaves out two floating S^(1)(eta_a) joined by a lambda-lambda edge P(eps,inf). This chain is allowed by Lemma o-legs (each floating odd vertex has one lambda leg and one A*|_V leg). Its superficial IR degree in R^8 is +1. eta_pair_ir.py works out the momentum-space symbol with explicit Euclidean sigma matrices. (1) The single-orientation degree -5 part is 4(eta1 pslash etabar2)/p^6, nonzero pointwise. (2) Wick signs plus graded symmetry of P(lambda lambda) give Total = C1[z,z'] - C1[z',z] + (1<->2), so the degree -5 part cancels identically. (3) The surviving degree -4 part has S^3 average 6i v1.(f0 g1 - f1 g0), with v1 = Gamma(eta1,eta2)|_V and (f0,f1), (g0,g1) the Taylor data of the rest of the cycle; the hand formula matches to 6e-15. (4) Shell integrals over rho<|p|<2rho with an exact (non-Taylor) Gaussian rest tend to 2pi^2 log2 * 6i v1.(f0 g1 - f1 g0) (relative deviation 5e-8 at rho = 1e-4). This is a genuine log R divergence, proportional in position space to the integral of v1.(z'-z) against the rest. For defect graphs the coefficient is O(eps), exactly as in K-route classes C, D. For O[inf]^(2)(eta1,eta2) and W^(2) it is O(1). For v1 = 0 the degree -4 part vanishes pointwise (max 6e-14 against 64 for a generic pair). Control: for (xi,eta) pairs the single-orientation log term cancels between orientations, so they converge.

flagged.evidence: hep-th/0501077v2. (101): K_10 = Z_K B + Z_O D^2O. (102): Z_K = 1 + g^2 m11/eps, 'we take Z_K to have minimal subtraction form' (a choice). (103): <K_10 Dbar^2 Obar> = O(eps). (106): n10 = -M/4, M = N/(4pi^2). (99): -2D^2O = F - 4B. Redefine the trilinear by B' = B + y g^2 (F - 4B); this has the same quantum numbers and is the project's F3 finite-part freedom. Then F - 4B' is still proportional to the protected operator, so (99) still holds, and orthogonality (103) now gives an F coefficient g^2N/(32pi^2) - y g^2. EJSS (2) says a(g), b(g) 'depend on the normalization of the operators, i.e. on the subtraction scheme'. EJSS (3) and the abstract: in the superconformal scheme [F]_R does not appear at all. EJSS fn 13: exactness of the classical field equations 'may be a scheme-dependent property'. Twisted side: sum Tr beta_I gamma^I is not Q_0-closed, so c_K is not part of pi_0 Q_1 iota_0. By the file's own Lemma inv it is therefore scheme dependent.
